name: Barna Group homepage: landing page of a Christian research organisation
title: Barna Group homepage: landing page of a Christian research organisation
answer: This is the homepage of Barna Group, a Christian research organisation that publishes data and insights on faith, culture and ministry. It is a landing page rather than a report, promoting a free webcast on six trends in pastoral leadership, The State of Pastors, Volume 2, a church leadership podcast and new data on why young adults attend church. The most useful thing it establishes is Barna's role as a survey-based research publisher for churches. It does not mention artificial intelligence anywhere.

sections.body: This is the homepage of Barna Group, which describes itself as a Christian research organization that provides data and insights on the trends affecting faith, culture and ministry today. It is a landing page rather than a research document, and it points visitors towards the organisation's articles, reports, podcasts, courses and services. The page was harvested on 26 September 2026. Its scope is promotional and navigational, covering a webcast, a report, a podcast series and a data item on church attendance, rather than presenting a single study in full.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page describes Barna Group as a Christian research organisation providing data and insights on the trends affecting faith, culture and ministry today, and invites visitors to explore its articles, reports, podcasts, courses and services. Much of the page promotes a free webcast replay about six trends shaping the future of pastoral leadership, tied to a new research report called The State of Pastors, Volume 2. That report is described as an in-depth look at how pastors are navigating post-pandemic life and ministry, organised around self-leadership, church leadership and cultural leadership. The page also promotes a podcast hosted by pastors Glenn Packiam, Rich Villodas and Sharon Hodde Miller, in which leaders discuss the challenges and opportunities of leading a church in a rapidly changing world, speaking with pastors, church leaders, thinkers and theologians about the health of the pastor, the state of the church and what it looks like to love well and lead faithfully. A further item notes that young adults are not showing up to church for just one reason, and that new Barna data breaks down the social motivators behind church attendance. The page contains no discussion of artificial intelligence, and no survey figures are presented.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, statistics or definitions. It names six trends shaping the future of pastoral leadership, a report titled The State of Pastors, Volume 2, and three podcast hosts, Glenn Packiam, Rich Villodas and Sharon Hodde Miller, but no survey results, percentages or sample sizes appear.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in churches and faith organisations would use this page mainly to locate the publisher rather than to learn anything about AI. It confirms that Barna Group positions itself as a research organisation producing data on faith, culture and ministry, and it shows the channels through which that work is released, namely reports, webcasts and podcasts. That makes the page a starting point for finding Barna's church research, but the harvested text itself offers no AI adoption, perception or usage findings, so it cannot support any claim about how congregations or ministry leaders are using AI.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Churches and Faith Organisations

sections.body: This is a commercial landing page promoting webcasts, reports, podcasts, courses and services, so it is promotional rather than evidential. It does not mention artificial intelligence, does not contain the State of the Church research, and presents no survey data or methodology. It is dated only by the harvest date, and the substance behind each promotion sits on other pages that this text does not include.
